decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding identify the same tested original study: Hickok, Farahbod, & Saberi (2015), 'The rhythm of perception: Entrainment to acoustic rhythms induces subsequent perceptual oscillation' (Psychological Science, DOI: 10.1177/0956797615576533). The paper explicitly states that it was designed to replicate and extend the entrainment findings of Hickok et al. (2015).

decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding record the replication outcome as failed. Across both new-sample experiments—Experiment 1 (conceptual replication, N = 24) and Experiment 2 (exact replication, N = 23)—the authors found no significant 3-Hz cyclic entrainment effect at the group level (whether analyzed via hit rate, restricted threshold-matched subsets, accuracy, or d-prime) and no consistent anti-phase alignment among the 36% participant subset showing positive modulation. The positive reanalysis of the original N = 5 dataset in Section 3.1 is a secondary calibration check on the original data, and the non-cyclic inverted-U foreperiod pattern in Section 3.4 is an alternative empirical phenomenon, so the overall replication verdict for Hickok et al. (2015) is failed.

decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding classify this study as a replication. Although Section 3.1 first re-analyzes the original N = 5 dataset from Hickok et al. (2015) with a modified analytical pipeline as a baseline reference, the main study collects and analyzes new experimental data from 47 participants across Experiment 1 (N = 24, conceptual replication) and Experiment 2 (N = 23, exact replication) to re-test Hickok et al.'s (2015) published finding.
